stem: The biological process of producing new individuals of the same kind is called __________.
solution: Reproduction produces new individuals and ensures the continuity of a species.

stem: Reproduction involving a single parent without gamete fusion is called __________ reproduction.
solution: Asexual reproduction involves one parent and produces genetically identical offspring.

stem: Reproduction involving two parents and the fusion of gametes is called __________ reproduction.
solution: Sexual reproduction involves two parents and the fusion of male and female gametes.

stem: Amoeba reproduces asexually by __________.
solution: Amoeba divides into two by binary fission.

stem: The malarial parasite Plasmodium reproduces by dividing into many cells at once, called __________.
solution: In multiple fission, the parent divides into many daughter cells at once, as in Plasmodium.

stem: Hydra and yeast reproduce asexually by __________.
solution: In budding, a small outgrowth develops on the parent and detaches to form a new individual.

stem: Spirogyra reproduces asexually by __________.
solution: Spirogyra breaks into fragments, each of which grows into a new organism.

stem: The regrowth of an entire organism from a body part, as in Planaria, is called __________.
solution: Regeneration is the ability of some organisms to regrow a full body from a fragment.

stem: Fungi like Rhizopus reproduce asexually by producing __________.
solution: Rhizopus (bread mould) reproduces by spores formed in structures called sporangia.

stem: The growth of new plants from vegetative parts such as roots, stems and leaves is called __________.
solution: Vegetative propagation is asexual reproduction from vegetative plant parts.

stem: Which of the following is a method of artificial vegetative propagation?
solution: Grafting, layering and cuttings are artificial methods of vegetative propagation.

stem: The technique of growing plants from a small tissue or cells in a nutrient medium is called __________.
solution: Tissue culture grows many plants from small tissue pieces in a laboratory, producing identical plants quickly.

stem: The male reproductive part of a flower is the __________.
solution: The stamen (anther + filament) is the male part, producing pollen.

stem: The female reproductive part of a flower is the __________.
solution: The pistil (stigma, style, ovary) is the female reproductive part.

stem: The transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma is called __________.
solution: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma.

stem: The fusion of the male gamete with the egg to form a zygote is called __________.
solution: Fertilisation is the fusion of the male and female gametes to form a zygote.

stem: After fertilisation, the ovule develops into a __________ and the ovary into a __________.
solution: The fertilised ovule becomes the seed and the ovary becomes the fruit.

stem: The male reproductive organs in humans that produce sperms are the __________.
solution: The testes produce sperms and the hormone testosterone.

stem: The female reproductive organs that produce eggs are the __________.
solution: The ovaries produce eggs and female hormones.

stem: In humans, fertilisation normally takes place in the __________.
solution: Fertilisation in humans usually occurs in the oviduct (fallopian tube).

stem: The fertilised egg (embryo) develops into a baby inside the __________.
solution: The embryo implants and develops in the uterus (womb).

stem: The structure that supplies nutrients and oxygen from the mother to the developing embryo is the __________.
solution: The placenta connects the embryo to the mother and enables exchange of nutrients, oxygen and wastes.

stem: The monthly cycle of shedding the uterine lining if fertilisation does not occur is called __________.
solution: Menstruation is the monthly shedding of the uterine lining when the egg is not fertilised.

stem: The first menstruation, marking the start of the reproductive phase, is called __________.
solution: Menarche is the first menstrual period in a girl.

stem: The permanent stopping of menstruation around 45–50 years is called __________.
solution: Menopause is the permanent cessation of menstruation in women.

stem: Methods used to prevent pregnancy are called __________ methods.
solution: Contraceptive methods prevent pregnancy and help in family planning.

stem: Barrier methods of contraception, like condoms, work by __________.
options: preventing the sperm from reaching the egg
solution: Barrier methods physically prevent sperm from meeting the egg.

stem: Oral contraceptive pills prevent pregnancy mainly by __________.
options: changing hormone balance to stop ovulation
solution: Oral pills alter hormonal balance, typically preventing the release of eggs (ovulation).

stem: Diseases spread through unsafe sexual contact, like HIV/AIDS and syphilis, are called __________.
solution: STIs (like HIV/AIDS, gonorrhoea, syphilis) can spread through unsafe sexual contact.

stem: Sexual reproduction leads to variation among offspring because they __________.
solution: Sexual reproduction combines genes from two parents, producing variation important for evolution.

stem: Variation is important for a species because it __________.
options: helps the species survive changing environments
solution: Variation gives raw material for natural selection, helping species adapt and survive changes.

stem: In flowering plants, the pollen grain forms a __________ to reach the ovule after landing on the stigma.
solution: After landing on the stigma, the pollen germinates and grows a pollen tube down to the ovule to deliver the male gamete.

stem: Which of the following reproduces by budding?
solution: Yeast and Hydra reproduce by budding.

stem: The potato reproduces vegetatively through its __________.
solution: The potato's stem tuber has buds ('eyes') that sprout into new plants.

stem: The Bryophyllum plant reproduces vegetatively through buds on its __________.
solution: Bryophyllum bears buds along the margins of its leaves, which grow into new plants.

stem: Asexual reproduction is advantageous because it __________.
options: is fast and needs only one parent
solution: Asexual reproduction is quick, needs only one parent, and produces identical offspring.

stem: The developing baby that has recognisable body parts is called a __________.
solution: When the embryo's body parts become identifiable, it is called a foetus.

stem: In humans, the sex of the child is determined by __________.
options: the sex chromosome from the father
solution: The father's sperm (X or Y chromosome) determines the sex of the child.

stem: The variation that arises during DNA copying in reproduction is the basis of __________.
solution: Small variations during DNA copying provide the raw material for evolution.

stem: Which of the following is a sexually transmitted bacterial disease?
solution: Syphilis and gonorrhoea are bacterial STIs; AIDS is viral.

stem: Reproductive health means being __________ with respect to reproduction.
solution: Reproductive health is the total well-being (physical, mental, social) related to reproduction.

stem: Grafting is a method in which __________.
options: a cutting of one plant is joined to a rooted stem of another
solution: In grafting, a stem cutting (scion) of one plant is joined to the rooted stem (stock) of another.

stem: Which of the following pairs an organism with its correct mode of reproduction?
solution: Plasmodium reproduces by multiple fission. (Amoeba–binary fission, Hydra–budding, Spirogyra–fragmentation.)

stem: The primary function of reproduction for a species is to __________.
solution: Reproduction ensures the species continues from one generation to the next.

stem: Which of the following contraceptive methods is a surgical one?
solution: Vasectomy (in males) and tubectomy (in females) are surgical (permanent) contraceptive methods.

stem: DNA copying during reproduction is important because it ensures that offspring __________.
options: inherit the characters of the parents (with small variations)
solution: DNA copying passes on parental characters to offspring, with small variations enabling evolution.

stem: A flower that has both stamens and pistil is called a __________ flower.
solution: A bisexual flower has both male (stamen) and female (pistil) reproductive parts.

stem: Sexual reproduction produces __________ among offspring.
solution: Sexual reproduction combines genes from two parents, producing variation.

stem: In humans, the embryo develops in the __________.
solution: The embryo develops into a baby in the uterus.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'How do Organisms Reproduce?' is that:
options: organisms reproduce asexually or sexually to continue their species, with sexual reproduction providing variation important for evolution, and reproductive health is essential
only one method of reproduction exists
solution: The chapter explains asexual and sexual reproduction in plants and animals, human reproduction, variation, contraception and reproductive health.

stem: The production of new individuals from their parents is called __________.
solution: Reproduction is the biological process of producing new individuals.

stem: Reproduction involving only one parent, without gametes, is called __________ reproduction.
solution: Asexual reproduction involves a single parent and no fusion of gametes.

stem: The division of a unicellular organism like Amoeba into two is called binary __________.
solution: In binary fission, the parent cell divides into two daughter cells, as in Amoeba.

stem: The type of asexual reproduction seen in Hydra, where a bud grows and detaches, is called __________.
solution: In budding, a new individual develops as an outgrowth (bud) on the parent, as in Hydra.

stem: The breaking of an organism into fragments that each grow into a new individual is called __________.
solution: Fragmentation, seen in Spirogyra, produces new organisms from body fragments.

stem: The ability of Planaria to grow into a full organism from a cut piece is called __________.
solution: Regeneration is the regrowth of a full organism from a body part, as in Planaria.

stem: Reproduction in fungi like Rhizopus by tiny reproductive units is called __________.
solution: Many fungi reproduce asexually by forming spores.

stem: Growing new plants from vegetative parts like roots, stems or leaves is called __________.
solution: Vegetative propagation produces new plants from vegetative parts without seeds.

stem: The fusion of the male and female gametes is called __________.
solution: Fertilisation is the fusion of male and female gametes to form a zygote.

stem: After fertilisation, the ovule develops into a __________.
solution: The fertilised ovule develops into a seed.

stem: After fertilisation, the ovary of a flower develops into a __________.
solution: The ovary develops into the fruit that encloses the seeds.

stem: The male gametes in humans are called __________.
solution: Sperms are the male gametes produced in the testes.

stem: The female gametes in humans are called __________.
solution: Ova (egg cells) are the female gametes produced in the ovaries.

stem: The male gametes in humans are produced in the __________.
solution: Sperms are produced in the testes.

stem: The female gametes in humans are produced in the __________.
solution: Ova are produced in the ovaries.

stem: The developing baby is nourished in the mother's uterus through the __________.
solution: The placenta provides nutrients and oxygen from mother to the developing embryo.

stem: The monthly release of an egg from the ovary is called __________.
solution: Ovulation is the release of a mature egg from the ovary each month.

stem: If the egg is not fertilised, the thickened uterine lining breaks down during __________.
solution: Menstruation is the shedding of the uterine lining when fertilisation does not occur.

stem: The use of a condom during intercourse also helps prevent the spread of __________.
solution: Condoms are a barrier method that also prevents sexually transmitted infections.

stem: AIDS is a sexually transmitted disease caused by a __________.
solution: AIDS is caused by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).

stem: Syphilis and gonorrhoea are sexually transmitted diseases caused by __________.
solution: Syphilis and gonorrhoea are bacterial sexually transmitted diseases.

stem: Grafting, layering and cutting are methods of __________.
solution: Grafting, layering and cutting are artificial methods of vegetative propagation.

stem: An advantage of vegetative propagation is that the new plants are __________ to the parent.
solution: Plants from vegetative propagation are genetically identical to the parent.

stem: Tissue culture produces many plants from a small amount of plant tissue grown in a __________.
solution: Tissue culture grows plant cells on a nutrient medium to produce many plantlets.

stem: Self-pollination occurs when pollen is transferred to the stigma of __________.
solution: Self-pollination transfers pollen within the same flower or plant.

stem: Cross-pollination occurs when pollen is transferred to the stigma of a flower on __________.
options: a different plant of the same kind
solution: Cross-pollination transfers pollen between different plants of the same species.

stem: The change in a caterpillar to an adult butterfly through distinct stages is called __________.
solution: Metamorphosis is the transformation through distinct larval stages to the adult form.

stem: Reproduction is important because it ensures the __________ of a species.
solution: Reproduction ensures the continuity of a species from generation to generation.

stem: Sexual reproduction leads to more __________ among offspring than asexual reproduction.
solution: Sexual reproduction combines genes from two parents, producing greater variation.

stem: The structure that carries pollen grains in a flower is the __________.
solution: The anther, part of the stamen, produces and holds pollen grains.
